title: Adal moves its capital to Aussa
description: Beaten back from the highlands, Imam Muhammad Gasa takes his state inland to Aussa, and the sultanate that emerges rules the Afar lowlands of today's Djibouti for centuries.

title: Treaty of Obock
description: Afar rulers cede Obock to France, giving Paris its first foothold on this coast.

title: French protectorate over Tadjoura
description: France signs protection treaties over Tadjoura and the neighbouring sultanates, the start of French Somaliland.

title: Djibouti city founded
description: The French lay out a new town on the south side of the Gulf of Tadjoura, which soon replaces Obock as the seat of the colony.

title: Railway to Addis Ababa begun
description: Work starts on the metre-gauge line from Djibouti towards the Ethiopian capital, which makes the port the country's lifeline.

title: Rallies to Free France
description: After years under a Vichy administration and a British blockade, French Somaliland joins Charles de Gaulle's Free French.

title: Constitutional referendum
description: Voters choose to stay an overseas territory within the French Community rather than seek independence.

title: Independence rejected in referendum
polity: French Territory of the Afars and the Issas
description: A second referendum keeps the territory French and it is renamed the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas.

title: Independence referendum
polity: French Territory of the Afars and the Issas
description: Voters now overwhelmingly approve independence, with Hassan Gouled Aptidon's league winning the accompanying election.

title: Independence
description: France ends its rule and the Republic of Djibouti is proclaimed with Hassan Gouled Aptidon as president.

title: IGAD founded
description: The Intergovernmental Authority on Development is set up by the Horn of Africa states with its headquarters in Djibouti.

title: Civil war
description: The Afar-led FRUD takes up arms against Issa dominance, and the army fights back for three years before peace accords split and absorb the rebels.

title: Guelleh elected president
description: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh succeeds his uncle Hassan Gouled Aptidon, the first peaceful handover of power in the country.

title: US base at Camp Lemonnier
description: The United States sets up Camp Lemonnier beside the airport; foreign bases become central to the state's economy.

title: Eritrean border clash
description: Eritrean and Djiboutian troops fight over the disputed Ras Doumeira headland at the entrance to the Red Sea.

title: Guelleh wins fourth term
description: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh is re-elected with a large majority, extending his rule past a quarter of a century.
